resources.string: Show the proposals of external models
No proposal is waiting. What a model proposes for this document shows here, and nothing changes until you accept it.
Add a text on a new page
Change the style of a text
Change the color or width of a stroke
Change the format of a page
This text changed after the model read it: it will not be overwritten.
Not applied: the text had changed
Let clients in on this device
Programs on this computer, like a coding assistant or a script, can read the documents you allow and change them. What they read goes to the model they use, under its terms.
A document can hold text written by others, even instructions meant to mislead a model: review what is proposed.
From a terminal, run “pencilnotes docs”. A client of the Model Context Protocol starts “pencilnotes mcp”.
Every document of the library, the ones made later too. Turned off, only the documents allowed one by one.
What a client proposes is applied when it arrives, without waiting for you. It can be undone.
Changed since: not undone, so that nothing written after it is lost.
Its document cannot be changed on this device.
A client can now change every document without asking. A document may hold instructions written to mislead a model: what it removes goes to the trash, and what it changes can be undone.
